rules.title: JVM or Android API in common code
rules.description: Common code is compiled for every target, so a reference to `java.`, `javax.` or `android.` (an import included) does not compile for iOS. Use a Kotlin standard or multiplatform library, or declare it with `expect`/`actual`.
rules.why: Common code that references `java.`, `javax.` or `android.` does not compile for iOS and the other non-JVM targets.
rules.fix: Use a Kotlin standard or multiplatform library, or move the call behind an `expect`/`actual` declaration.

rules.title: Public common function that can throw without @Throws
rules.description: A public function in common code can throw but has no `@Throws`: Swift cannot catch the exception and the app crashes. It is a BLOCKER when the function is called from Swift.

rules.title: Common API hard to use from Swift
rules.description: A public API in common code that Swift consumes awkwardly: `suspend` functions and `Flow` without a wrapper, default arguments, sealed interfaces, variance or value classes. Expose a Swift-friendly shape for what the iOS app calls.

rules.title: expect declaration without an actual
rules.description: An `expect` declaration needs an `actual` in every target source set, or the module does not compile for that target. An `expect` declaration added or changed under `src/commonMain` is a candidate when `androidMain`, `iosMain` or `jvmMain` of its module has files and no `actual` with the same package, name and kind, neither in the change request nor on the target branch. Judge whether the actual lives in another source set of the hierarchy, such as a per-target ios one.
rules.why: The module does not compile for the target that has no `actual`, so its build fails.
rules.fix: Add the matching `actual` declaration to the platform source set, or to the intermediate source set the target depends on.

rules.title: Behaviour changed in one source set only
rules.description: A change in one platform source set without the matching change in the others, so the targets behave differently. A file changed under `androidMain`, `iosMain`, `iosArm64Main`, `iosX64Main`, `iosSimulatorArm64Main` or `jvmMain` whose counterpart in another platform source set (platform suffix such as `.android` stripped) exists and is not changed is a candidate; judge whether the change is deliberately platform-specific.
rules.why: The targets now behave differently: the same call does one thing on one platform and another on the others.
rules.fix: Make the matching change in the other platform source sets, or state why the behaviour is meant to differ.

rules.title: Missing unit tests of shared code
rules.description: Unit tests for every repository, use case, mapper or helper added or changed in the shared code. It is checked on the whole change request, not on one file: a source under `src/commonMain` named with one of the suffixes needs a test named `<Name>Test` in the change request or under `src/commonTest`, `src/androidUnitTest` or `src/iosTest` of its module. Dismiss the signal when the component has no logic to test.
rules.why: The shared component has no unit test, so regressions in its logic cannot be detected on any target before release.
rules.fix: Add a unit test for the component under the module's `src/commonTest`, or under a platform test source set when it needs one.
